slides.title: Inline Functions Overview
slides.prompt: The 'inline' keyword hints to the compiler to substitute function calls directly with the function's machine code, eliminating call overhead at the expense of binary size.

slides.title: Inline Keyword Placement
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword to request function code substitution.

slides.title: Compiler Inlining Authority
slides.prompt: Is the 'inline' keyword a strict mandatory command to the C++ compiler?
options: No, it is merely a recommendation; the compiler decides whether to inline based on optimization settings
Yes, the compiler must inline every function marked inline
Yes, but only in debug build modes
No, inline is deprecated in C++20
slides.correctAnswer: No, it is merely a recommendation; the compiler decides whether to inline based on optimization settings

slides.title: Implicit Inlining in Classes
slides.prompt: Functions defined inside class declarations are implicitly marked ___. Fill in keyword.

slides.title: Inline Linkage Exception
slides.prompt: What key linkage permission does the 'inline' keyword grant regarding multiple definitions?
options: Allows identical function definitions in multiple header-included translation units without linker errors
Restricts function access strictly to the local source file
Makes the function globally accessible to C programs
Forces function symbols to be dynamically exported
slides.correctAnswer: Allows identical function definitions in multiple header-included translation units without linker errors

slides.title: Inline Variables in C++17
slides.prompt: Fill in the C++17 keyword that permits global constants in headers without violating ODR.

slides.title: Drawbacks of Over-Inlining
slides.prompt: What is the primary risk of forcing inlining on large complex functions?
options: Code bloat causing instruction cache misses and performance loss
Memory leak on the call stack
slides.correctAnswer: Code bloat causing instruction cache misses and performance loss

slides.title: Always Inline Compiler Extensions
slides.prompt: Fill in MSVC attribute keyword for forcing inline substitution.

slides.title: Inlining and Recursion
slides.prompt: Can recursive functions be completely inlined at compile time?
options: Generally no, because call depth is dynamic (unless unrolled for fixed depth compile-time limits)
Yes, recursive functions are always inlined
slides.correctAnswer: Generally no, because call depth is dynamic (unless unrolled for fixed depth compile-time limits)

slides.title: Header Placement for Inline Functions
slides.prompt: Inline function definitions must be placed in ___ files so compilers see the body in every translation unit.
